analyzed_vuln.description: The bug is a length/encoding mismatch for GlyphID text. In textToGlyphIDs(), when paint encoding is kGlyphID_TextEncoding, it returns a span over the raw input bytes as uint16_t glyph IDs using byteLength/2 (floor). This permits odd byteLength (non-multiple of 2) to propagate. Later GPU text path (GrTextContext::DrawBmpPosText -> SkFindAndPlaceGlyph::ProcessPosText -> GlyphIdGlyphFinder::nextGlyphId in skia/src/core/SkFindAndPlaceGlyph.h) iterates glyphs by repeatedly reading 2 bytes from a char* stream without validating remaining bytes, causing a 2-byte read past the end on the final odd trailing byte.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From api_mock_gpu_canvas, fuzzed drawing commands reach drawPosTextH/drawText with SkPaint set to kGlyphID_TextEncoding and attacker-controlled text pointer/byteLength. If byteLength is odd (e.g., 5), SkGlyphRunBuilder::textToGlyphIDs accepts it (span count=2 glyphs) but downstream playback/reprocessing uses the original text byte stream and consumes 2-byte glyph IDs until text<stop, so the last iteration dereferences a uint16_t starting at the final single byte. This triggers heap-buffer-overflow in GlyphIdGlyphFinder::nextGlyphId.
